CGI Artist Brings Back the Volkswagen Santana Sedan and Wagon From the Dead, Though Only Virtually
8 photos
Photo: zijie8783 / Instagram
The German automaker Volkswagen has been pretty busy recently in America and Europe, where it launched important models like the 328-hp T-Roc R and, at the Los Angeles Auto Show, presented the Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport family together for the first time alongside the US-exclusive Rabbit Edition for the VW Golf GTI.
All these are fine and dandy, but Volkswagen is falling behind the competition in North America where it offers fewer and fewer models – the electric ID.4 is getting retired soon, and there’s no telling when the all-new ID. Tiguan is coming to the US to replace it. Otherwise, VW sells the all-new Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport plus the Tiguan and Taos as crossover SUVs.
Meanwhile, the passenger car line has just a couple of entries – the compact VW Golf GTI and R hatchbacks of the sporty and hot variety, plus the traditional compact Jetta sedan. Quite obviously, Volkswagen could do better with an additional nameplate or two. Well, here’s a suggestion coming from across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI thanks to a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators.
More precisely, Zijie Yang, a virtual designer better known as ' zijie8783 ' on social media, is actually an Exterior Designer at XPeng, so we'd better pay attention to what he CGIs. On this occasion, the pixel master suggests that Volkswagen should bring back the classic Santana nameplate – and perhaps even sell it in North America.
The original was a series of sedans and station wagon models offered by Volkswagen as an alternative to the Passat nameplate. It was offered since 1981 and also had other names – like the Quantum in North America, Corsar in Mexico, and Carat in Argentina. Production ended the latest in 2022 in China, while Europe hasn’t seen it since 1984 and Latin America since 2006.
Anyway, the CGI expert’s proposal for a revival is tugging at the heartstrings of nostalgia, featuring the styling elements of the 1980s reinterpreted in modern fashion – the dual square headlights are smaller and LED, plus there’s also a dual-tone paint with ‘chrome’ on the bottom half and the grille, plus a squared profile that harkens back to the boxy style of the 1980s.
The wide taillights are now full-width LEDs, and the author crafted both sedan and station wagon versions. The saloon, for example, dressed in silver and blue, is a sportier option with an all-electric powertrain, featuring a black front splitter and a rear diffuser along with black wheels. The station wagon, meanwhile, has pixel-style LED headlights and matching silver wheels along with a silver-and-black treatment. Plus, it’s clearly ICE -powered, as hinted by the dual rear exhaust.
